Text 1
Flash Fiction: Writing a Story in 1,000 Words or Less
[1] People have been enjoying stories for as long as humanity has been around.
Some people love to read 400-page novels, while others struggle to read the first
four paragraphs. More and more, technology has unfortunately resulted in many
people having shorter attention spans. Therefore, writers have to find new ways
to tell stories in a way that appeals to people who are used to reading snippets of
information on the small screen of their smart phones. Flash fiction is a medium
that works perfectly in a low-attention-span world.
What is Flash Fiction?
[2] Flash fiction is a category of short story that limits the author to a word
count of 1,000 words or less. Some magazines limit flash fiction stories to as
little as 300 words.
How to Write Flash Fiction
[3] Following the tips below will guide you in writing a solid flash fiction story.
Focus on One Character
[4] With a limit of 1,000 words, there isn’t a lot of room for character
development, so you’ll want to pick one character to focus on. There will likely
be two characters in the story because you’ll often use a human antagonist as
opposition to your main character. You might be able to use three characters,
but any more than that will probably be overkill in the realm of flash fiction.

Focus on One Scene
[5] Longer story forms have a beginning, middle, and end, but with flash
fiction, you’re really telling only the end of a story. Of course, you won’t be able
to flesh out a complex story world. Instead, your flash fiction story should focus
on one scene, one moment in the life of your character. It needs to be a
significant, life-altering moment for your character. Focusing on one scene also
means focusing on one location. So for flash fiction your limited word count
focuses on the essentials to the story.
Focus on One Conflict
[6] All stories are about conflict. A story can be easily defined as a character who
wants or needs something and has to overcome some obstacle in order to attain
it. The obstacle is the conflict. You have to answer two very important questions
to write a really good flash fiction story:
1. What does your main character want?
2. Who or what is trying to stop your main character from getting it?
Focus on One Theme
[7] Your theme is the moral argument of your story. It’s about how you want
your readers to be impacted by the story. What do you want them to be
encouraged to do, be, or believe as a result of reading your story?
Focus on Word Choice
[8] You only have up to 1,000 words to tell your story, so you have to choose
those words wisely. When you know what actions and ideas you want to
communicate, choose the least amount of words to communicate them.

How Flash Fiction Makes You a Better Writer
[9] Flash fiction forces you to be economical with your words. It helps you to
focus your ideas and strip away anything that isn’t essential to your story.
Often, when you’re writing flash fiction, you’ll write more than you need. When
you go back through, you’ll see what needs to be there, what can be taken out,
and what needs to be reworked, which helps you to develop your editing and
revising skills.
Flash Fiction Example
The Big Bang
[10] BOOOOOOOOOMMMM!!!! Timothy’s eyes nearly popped out of his
head. His face was blackened with soot and his hair stood on end. He looked
down at what remained of the school laboratory bench and saw smouldering
wood and shattered glass. Shocked faces gazed up at him.

[11] A month ago, it had all started fairly well. It was nearly the end of
Chemistry and Timothy was drifting in a pleasant doze with his head rested
upon Super Science Experiments for Eager Youngsters, whilst Professor
Snookhorn droned on. “So, if anyone is interested, raise your hand now … how
about you Timothy?” “Eh? Ermmm – sure,” mumbled Timothy with not the
faintest idea of what he had been asked. “Marvellous!” replied an enthused
Professor Snookhorn, fixing him with a steely gaze through his thick glasses.
“Meet me in Lab 922 after school today and we’ll get started.” The bell clanged
and the students crashed out of the classroom like a herd of elephants. Billy
Brenton, class thug, barged past Timothy muttering “Swotty boy - volunteering
for Young Scientist of the Year - urghh!” “Arggghhhh!” thought Timothy, but it
was too late.
[12] Four weeks and 25 excruciating extra Chemistry lessons later, Timothy was
blinking out nervously at a gaggle of eager science teachers and pushy parents,
crammed into the National School of Science Laboratory for what Professor
Snookhorn enthusiastically described as “The pinnacle of my teaching career”
(no pressure).
[13] Professor Snookhorn was a superlative scientist but little did he know that
Timothy was a bigger hazard than sulphuric acid when it came to Chemistry.
He had mistaken Timothy’s glazed expression for wide-eyed enthusiasm in class.
Timothy looked down at the glistening bench, taking in the jewel-coloured
containers of liquids and crystals, without a clue of what they were or how to
use them.

Section Heading（小標題）
Topic（主題）
What is Flash Fiction?
甚麼是閃小說？
Paragraph 2
Definition（定義）
Flash fiction is a category of short story that limits the author to a word count
of 1,000 words or less.
閃小說是一種短篇故事類型，限制作者只能使用 1,000 字或更少的篇幅。

Paragraph 5
Contrast（對比）
Longer story forms have a beginning, middle, and end, but with flash fiction,
you’re really telling only the end of a story.
較長的故事形式會有開端、發展和結局，但在閃小說中，你其實只是在講述
一個故事的結尾。
Limitation（限制）
Of course, you won’t be able to flesh out a complex story world.
當然，你不可能完整鋪展一個複雜的故事世界。
Advice（建議）
Instead, your flash fiction story should focus on one scene, one moment in the
life of your character.
相反，你的閃小說應該集中於一個場景，也就是角色生命中的某一個時刻。
Elaboration（闡述）
It needs to be a significant, life-altering moment for your character.
這個時刻必須對角色而言十分重要，甚至足以改變其人生。
Explanation（解釋）
Focusing on one scene also means focusing on one location.
集中描寫一個場景，也意味著集中描寫一個地點。
Conclusion（結論）
So for flash fiction your limited word count focuses on the essentials to the
story.
因此，在閃小說中，有限的字數應該集中用於故事最關鍵的部分。

Section Heading（小標題）
Topic（主題）
How Flash Fiction Makes You a Better Writer
閃小說如何令你成為更好的作家
Paragraph 9（第九段）
Main Point（重點）
Flash fiction forces you to be economical with your words.
閃小說迫使你用字精簡。
Elaboration（闡述）
It helps you to focus your ideas and strip away anything that isn’t essential to
your story.
它幫助你集中思想，並刪去任何對故事而言並非必要的內容。
Explanation（解釋）
Often, when you’re writing flash fiction, you’ll write more than you need.
通常，當你寫閃小說時，你會寫得比實際需要更多。
Elaboration（闡述）
When you go back through, you’ll see what needs to be there, what can be taken
out, and what needs to be reworked, which helps you to develop your editing
and revising skills.

這篇文章的核心可以分成3條線：
第一條線是「flash fiction 為甚麼適合現代讀者」。
文章一開始說，人類很早已經喜歡故事，但現代科技令很多人習慣看短小資
訊，專注時間變短。於是作家需要用新的方式說故事。Flash fiction 篇幅短，最
多 1000 字，所以很適合現代低專注力的閱讀環境。
第二條線是「flash fiction 如何靠限制產生力量」。
文章不斷重複一個概念：字數少，所以要集中。集中一個主角、一個場景、一
個衝突、一個主題，並且非常小心地選字。這種限制不但沒有削弱故事，反而
迫使作家刪走多餘部分，留下最重要的內容。
第三條線是「The Big Bang 如何展示 flash fiction 的特色」。
Timothy 的故事很短，主角集中，衝突清晰，笑點和高潮集中在一次爆炸。故
事看似荒謬，其實非常配合前面說的 flash fiction 原則：字數少、角色少、衝突
單一、結局有強烈轉折。

A. as big as 為甚麼不成立
A 把比較方向變成「大小」。
原文沒有說故事和人類一樣大，
故事也不能用 big 來和 human race 比較。
這是語義類別錯誤。題目要的是 age / history，A 給的是 size。
C. as long as 為甚麼很有誘惑力
C 最容易吸引學生，
因為原文真的有 “as long as humanity has been around”。
但摘要句的語法變成 “Stories are as long as the human race”，
這會令意思變成故事和人類 (身長) 一樣「長」?
這在英文中不自然，而且沒有準確表達「歷史久遠」
這是典型 keyword trap：
原文有相同字，不代表放到新句子就正確。

第(iv)行不是孤立一句。它的語法跨到第(v)行，
所以必須把整句讀完整：
However, unless you feel the need to have any more than this, your story will be
too long...
這句的表面意思是：
「除非你覺得需要有比這更多的角色，否則你的故事會太長。」
換成更清楚的邏輯：
如果你沒有想加入更多角色，你的故事會太長。
只有在你想加入更多角色的情況下，故事才可能避開太長這個問題。
這個意思很怪，
因為原文的意思剛好相反。
原文不是說「不加入更多角色會出問題」。
原文說的是「加入超過三個角色會出問題」。
所以 summary 用 unless，會把條件方向扭歪。

錯法三：把 “end” 理解得太字面，覺得故事怎可能只有結尾
有些學生會覺得：
如果只講 end，故事還完整嗎？
Flash fiction 再短也應該有 beginning 和 middle 吧？
所以 end 好像太奇怪。
這個想法很常見，也很合理，但它沒有跟原文的寫作理論對齊。
作者不是在說 flash fiction 完全沒有任何背景。
作者的意思是：
flash fiction 不會像長篇故事那樣慢慢鋪開完整的 beginning-middle-end。
它通常把讀者直接帶到故事已經累積到最後的關鍵時刻。
讀者看到的是那個 decisive moment，即決定人物命運或故事意義的一刻。
這和後面一句完全呼應：
your flash fiction story should focus on one scene, one moment in the life of
your character
也就是說，end 不是普通「最後一句」。
end 是故事發展中最重要、最有改變力的一刻。

先看題目問甚麼
這題是 pronoun reference 題。它問代詞 it 回指哪個名詞或概念。
這類題不能只看最近的名詞，還要看動作關係是否合理。
因為英文代詞有時候最接近的名詞未必是正確所指，
真正答案要同時符合語法和意思。
原文定位
第6段：
“A story can be easily defined as a character who wants or needs something and has
to overcome some obstacle in order to attain it.”
句子拆開來看：
a character wants or needs something
has to overcome some obstacle
in order to attain it
attain = get / achieve / obtain，意思是得到。
所以 it 指的是 something，即角色想要或需要的東西。

為甚麼 it 指 something
如果角色 wants or needs something，
接著又要 overcome obstacle in order to attain it，最自然的理解是：
角色想得到某樣東西
有障礙阻止他
他要克服障礙
才能得到那樣東西
所以 it = something the character wants or needs。
為甚麼 it 不指 obstacle
obstacle 是障礙。角色要 overcome obstacle，不會 attain obstacle
overcome 和 attain 是兩個不同動作：
overcome = 克服
attain = 得到
角色克服的是 obstacle，得到的是目標。
這是語義搭配問題。

為甚麼 it 不指 conflict
下一句說：“The obstacle is the conflict.”
conflict 是阻礙或問題本身，不是角色追求的目標。
角色一般不會想得到 conflict。
角色要解決 conflict 或克服 conflict!
常見誤讀
很多學生做 pronoun reference 題時，只找代詞前面最近的名詞。
這裡 it 前面最近的是 obstacle，但如果代入：
“overcome some obstacle in order to attain the obstacle”
意思很怪。角色不會為了得到障礙而克服障礙。
所以這題要看動詞搭配。
attain 只能合理連到 something wanted / needed。
Edmund Reading 技巧
代詞題三步走：
第一，向前找可能指代的名詞。
第二，代入原句，看語法是否通順。
第三，代入原句，看意思是否合理。
這題代入後最合理的是：
attain something the character wants or needs

陷阱類型
dramatic irony trap 戲劇反諷陷阱
讀者知道一件事。
人物相信另一件事。
答題時要回答人物當時相信的原因，但不能把他的誤會變成客觀事實。
Edmund Reading 技巧
人物心理題要問三個問題：
這個人物知道甚麼？
這個人物以為發生了甚麼？
讀者是否知道更多？
如果人物知識和讀者知識不同，
答案要用 “appeared to / seemed to / he believed” 這類語氣會更準確。

How to section

Focus on One Character
原文說 flash fiction 要 focus on one character，
因為 1000 字內沒有太多空間發展角色。
它也說故事 likely 有兩個角色，因為可能有 antagonist。
它再說 might be able to use three characters，但 any more than that will probably be
overkill。

原文說 flash fiction 應該 focus on one scene, one moment, one location。

Not Good Evidence 2：story describes more than one scene
Paragraph 5 說 flash fiction should focus on one scene, one moment, one location。
The Big Bang 至少寫了兩個明顯場景：
第一個場景：Chemistry classroom
Timothy 在 Chemistry 課打瞌睡，迷糊答應老師，Billy 嘲笑他。
第二個場景：National School of Science Laboratory / competition scene
Timothy 參加比賽，亂混材料，造成爆炸，最後得獎。
所以從嚴格角度看，故事不是 one scene / one location。
為甚麼這證據很強
因為它直接對應 “Focus on One Scene”。
The “How to” section 說：
focusing on one scene also means focusing on one location.
The Big Bang 有 classroom，也有 science laboratory。
兩個地點、兩個時間段，所以可說不完全符合 one-scene requirement。

body: 為甚麼不用
A. Parents
Parents 在故事裡有作用：
they are pushy parents
they watch the competition
they start to point
但三句 comments 中沒有一句主要對應 parents。
他們沒有嘲笑 Timothy 是 teacher’s pet。
他們沒有教導 Timothy，也沒有 “for us both” 的共同成就。
他們沒有被 Professor Snookhorn 誤會成懂化學的人。
所以 A 不用。

True 看支持，False 看相反，NG 看核心聲稱有沒有被提及。
第17題訓練 即時原因定位：
人物驚慌的原因要看當下視線與附近現象，不要把後面爆炸提前。
第18題訓練 直接原因與背景原因分辨：
爆炸的直接原因是 random mixing，不是「他不懂化學」這種背景。
第19題訓練 人物視角與讀者視角分辨：
Snookhorn proud 是因為他以為 Timothy 成功，讀者知道真相更荒謬。
第20題訓練 倒敘時間線重建：
故事先寫爆炸，不代表爆炸最早發生。要跟 one month ago、later 時間信號排
第21題訓練 按標準評價：
不能只說故事有趣，要用 How to section 的標準作證據。
第22題訓練 人物語氣與代詞關係配對：
teacher’s pet、for us both、I’m clueless 這些語氣和代詞都是判斷關鍵。
